'''''Encephalartos woodii''''', '''Wood's cycad''', is a rare [[cycad]] in the genus ''[[Encephalartos]]'', and is [[endemic (ecology)|endemic]] to the [[oNgoye Forest]] of [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[South Africa]]. It is one of the rarest plants in the world, being [[extinct in the wild]] with all [[Biological specimen|specimen]]s being [[cloning|clones]] of the [[type specimen|type]].<ref name="Jones"/> The specific and [[common name]] both honour [[John Medley Wood]], curator of the [[Durban Botanic Garden]] and director of the [[Natal Government Herbarium]] of South Africa, who discovered the plant in 1895.<ref name="Kew">{{cite web |title=Encephalartos woodii |url=http://www.kew.org.uk/plants/cycads/encephalartos_woodii.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101230151726/http://www.kew.org/plants/cycads/encephalartos_woodii.html |archive-date=2010-12-30 |access-date=2006-11-16 |work=Cycads |publisher=[[Kew Botanical Gardens]]}}</ref>

==Description==
It is [[palm tree]] like, and can reach a height of {{convert|6|m}}. The trunk is about {{convert|30|–|50|cm}} in diameter, thickest at the bottom, and topped by a crown of 50–150 leaves. The [[leaf|leaves]] are glossy and dark green, {{convert|150|–|250|cm}} in length, and keeled with 70–150 [[leaflet (botany)|leaflets]], the leaflets falcate (sickle-shaped), {{convert|13|–|15|cm|sigfig=1}} long and {{convert|20|–|30|mm|sigfig=1}} broad.<ref name="Plantzafrica">{{cite web |author=Notten |first=Alice |name-list-style=vanc |date=May 2002 |title=''Encephalartos woodii'' Sander |url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantefg/encephwoodii.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061016180523/http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantefg/encephwoodii.htm |archive-date=16 October 2006 |access-date=2006-11-16 |publisher=Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden and South African National Biodiversity Institute}}</ref><ref name="Cycadpages">{{cite web |author=Hill |first=K |name-list-style=vanc |year=2004 |title=''Encephalartos woodii'' |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/cycadpg?taxname=Encephalartos+woodii |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200221193323/http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/cycadpg?taxname=Encephalartos+woodii |archive-date=21 February 2020 |access-date=2006-12-01 |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Sydney}}</ref>

''E. woodii'' is [[Plant sexuality|dioecious]], meaning it has separate male and female plants; however, no female plant has ever been discovered. The male [[strobilus|strobili]] are cylindrical, {{convert|20|–|40|cm|sigfig=2}} long, exceptionally up to {{convert|120|cm}}, and {{convert|15|–|25|cm|sigfig=1}} in diameter; they are a vivid yellow-orange colour. A single plant may bear from around six to eight simultaneously.<ref name=Plantzafrica/><ref name=Cycadpages/>

==Taxonomy==
''Encephalartos woodii'' was first described by Wood as a [[variety (biology)|variety]] of ''[[Encephalartos altensteinii|E. altensteinii]]'' (as ''E. altensteinii'' var. ''bispinna''), and raised to the rank of species in 1908 by the English horticulturalist [[Henry Frederick Conrad Sander|Henry Sander]]<ref name=Cycadpages/> from studying a specimen in his collection, which was apparently one of the basal offsets taken from the original clump.<ref name="Jones"/> It has been considered that ''Encephalartos woodii'' is most closely related to ''[[Encephalartos natalensis|E. natalensis]]''. Some authorities consider ''E. woodii'' to not be a true [[species]] but rather a [[mutant]] ''E. natalensis'' or a [[Relict species|relict]] of some other species. Yet others consider this plant to be a [[natural hybrid]] between ''E. natalensis'' and ''[[Encephalartos ferox|E. ferox]]''.<ref name="Plantzafrica"/> To determine the relationship between ''E. natalensis'' and ''E. woodii'', the [[Random amplification of polymorphic DNA|RAPD]] technique was used to generate genetic fingerprints and data analysed using distance methods. Based on RAPD fingerprints, the [[intraspecific competition|intraspecific]] genetic variation among different ''E. natalensis'' plants is similar to the [[interspecific competition|interspecific]] variation between ''E. natalensis'' and ''E. woodii'', which confirms the close relationship between ''E. natalensis'' and ''E. woodii''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Viljoen |first=C.D. |last2=van Staden |first2=J. |name-list-style=vanc |date=2006 |title=The genetic relationship between Encephalartos natalensis and E. woodii determined using RAPD fingerprinting |journal=[[South African Journal of Botany]] |volume=72 |issue=4 |pages=642–645 |doi=10.1016/j.sajb.2006.03.008 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==

===Original distribution===
The only known wild plants of ''E. woodii'' were a cluster of four stems of one plant discovered by Wood in 1895 in a small area of [[Ngoya Forest]],<ref name="Remarkable-51">{{cite book |author=Esterhuyse |first=Neels |title=Remarkable Trees of South Africa |author2=von Breitenbach |first2=Jutta |author3=Söhnge |first3=Hermien |publisher=Briza Publications |year=2001 |isbn=1-875093-28-1 |editor=Ferreira |editor-first=Reneé |location=Pretoria, South Africa |page=51 |name-list-style=vanc}}<!--|access-date=2008-11-21--></ref> now known by its proper [[Zulu language|Zulu]] name of ''oNgoye'', which is in [[KwaZulu-Natal]], South Africa.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife |url=https://www.kznwildlife.com/ |access-date=2010-09-07}}</ref> The site where this plant was found was on a steep south-facing slope<ref name="Jones">{{Cite book |last=Jones |first=David L. |title=Cycads of the World: Ancient Plants in Today's Landscape |publisher=Reed |year=1993 |isbn=978-0-7301-0338-7 |edition=1st |location=Chatswood, NSW Australia |oclc=1409004984 |name-list-style=vanc}}</ref><ref name="Plantzafrica" /> on the fringes of the forest.<ref name="Plantzafrica" /> The annual rainfall at the site ranges between {{convert|750|–|1000|mm}}, and the climate has hot summers and mild winters.<ref name="Jones"/>

===Removal from natural habitat===
A basal offset of the main stems was removed and sent to [[Kew Gardens]] in 1899.<ref name="Jones"/> Three basal offsets were collected by Wood's deputy, [[James Wylie (botanist)|James Wylie]], in 1903 and planted in the [[Durban Botanic Garden]]s.<ref name="Plantzafrica" /> One specimen was received at the [[National Botanic Gardens (Ireland)|National Botanic Gardens of Ireland]] in [[Glasnevin]] in 1905<ref name="CzechCycads">Czech Cycads: Cycads in Ireland: http://www.cykasy.cz/English/Cycads_in_Ireland.html, retrieved 20 September 2010.</ref> where the register records it as "''Encephalartos way of E. Alten[steinii]''" costing 1 [[Guinea (British coin)|guinea]] from [[Henry Frederick Conrad Sander|Sander & Sons]].<ref name="Glasnevin">National Botanical Gardens, Glasnevin: Conservation News: http://www.botanicgardens.ie/conserve/consnews.htm {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110709213717/http://www.botanicgardens.ie/conserve/consnews.htm |date=9 July 2011 }}, retrieved 20 September 2010.</ref> In a 1907 expedition, Wylie collected two of the larger stems and noted that of the remaining two, one of them (the largest of the four original stems) was badly mutilated and he did not expect it to survive.<ref name="Plantzafrica" /> By 1912 there was only one {{convert|3|m}} tall trunk left in the wild, and in 1916, the Forestry Department arranged to have it removed and sent to the Government Botanist in [[Pretoria]].<ref name="Plantzafrica" /> It is thought that this trunk subsequently died in 1964.<ref name="Plantzafrica" />

===Current distribution===
While extinct in the wild, ''Encephalartos woodii'' specimens are found in many botanical gardens, institutions and collections around the world, with an estimated 500 individuals in existence, all clones of the original specimen.<ref name="Jones"/><ref name="PlantZAfrika">{{cite web |last=Notten |first=Alice |name-list-style=vanc |date=May 2002 |title=''Encephalartos woodii'' Sander |url=https://pza.sanbi.org/encephalartos-woodii |access-date=2 August 2023 |website=PlantZAfrika |publisher=[[South African National Biodiversity Institute|SANBI]]}}</ref> For an ''Encephalartos'' cycad, ''E. woodii'' is relatively fast-growing and vigorous in cultivation.<ref name=PlantZAfrika/>

Two of the larger trunks that Wylie collected in the 1907 expedition are still to be seen in the Durban Botanic Gardens.<ref name="Plantzafrica" /> A sucker from one of the Durban Botanic Gardens plants was sent to [[Kirstenbosch]] near [[Cape Town]], South Africa in 1916 by James Wylie.<ref name="Plantzafrica" /> The plant that was sent to Kew Gardens in 1899 was grown in the Palm House until April 1997 and then moved to the Temperate House where it produced, for the first time, a male cone in September 2004.<ref name="Kew" /> Other European specimens include one housed at [[Hortus Botanicus (Amsterdam)|Hortus Botanicus]] in [[Amsterdam]], the Netherlands,<ref>{{cite web |title=Belangrijke collecties |url=https://www.dehortus.nl/de-tuin/belangrijke-collecties/ |publisher=Hortus Botanicus |access-date=9 September 2024}}</ref> and one in [[Orto Botanico di Napoli]] in Italy,<ref>Los Gatos Plants - UK Cycad Resource: {{cite web |url=https://losgatosplants.blogspot.com/2009/10/cycads-of-orto-botanico-naples.html |title=Blogger: Anmelden |access-date=2010-09-14 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120701014614/https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?service=blogger&hl=de&passive=86400&continue=http://www.blogger.com/blogin.g%3FblogspotURL%3Dhttp://losgatosplants.blogspot.de/2009/10/cycads-of-orto-botanico-naples.html%26zx%3D1blk6njs4o9z&ltmpl=private |archive-date=1 July 2012 }}, retrieved 14 September 2010.</ref> although this specimen may have died. The specimen in Ireland at [[National Botanic Gardens (Ireland)|Glasnevin]] is said to be "probably the tallest" specimen of ''E. woodii'' in Europe.<ref name="CzechCycads"/> In the United States, a specimen is housed in the conservatory at [[Longwood Gardens]] near [[Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania<ref>{{cite web |title=Rare Plants in Pennsylvania. Wood's Cycad. Encephalartos woodii |url=http://www.frenchtowner.com/Rare-Plants-in-Pennsylvania-.-Woods-Cycad-.-Encephalartos-woodii.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100814031402/http://www.frenchtowner.com/Rare-Plants-in-Pennsylvania-.-Woods-Cycad-.-Encephalartos-woodii.html |archive-date=14 August 2010 |access-date=2010-09-14 |website=frenchtowner.com}}</ref> and three specimens are to be seen at [[Lotusland]] in [[Santa Barbara, California]]<ref name="Lotusland">{{Cite web |title=Cycad Garden |url=http://www.lotusland.org/explore-garden/gardens/cycad-garden/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230010007/http://www.lotusland.org/explore-garden/gardens/cycad-garden/ |archive-date=2014-12-30 |access-date=2010-09-14 |website=Lotusland |publisher=Ganna Walska}}</ref> where they were planted in 1979.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Compiled List of Cycad Gardens |url=http://www.plantapalm.com/vce/cycadsof/cycadgardens.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717093038/http://www.plantapalm.com/vce/cycadsof/cycadgardens.htm |archive-date=17 July 2011 |access-date=14 September 2010 |website=plantapalm.com}}</ref> The specimen at Longwood Gardens was received in 1969 after a request was made to the Durban Botanic Gardens by one of Longwood's former directors, [[Dr. Russell Seibert]], when he went on a plant exploration voyage to South Africa in the 1960s.<ref name="Longwood">{{Cite web |last=Longwood Gardens |date=2010-01-25 |title=The King of Our Conservatory |url=https://www.facebook.com/note.php?note_id=296456165465 |access-date=2010-09-14 |website=facebook.com}}</ref> The rooted plant was first taken to the Research Department at Longwood where the gardeners nurtured the plant until it was ready to be displayed in the Conservatory.<ref name="Longwood"/> The Longwood specimen produces cones in early winter.<ref name="Longwood"/>

==Conservation status==
Despite numerous excursions in the oNgoye-[[Mtunzini]] area, no other specimens of ''Encephalartos woodii'' have ever been found. All known specimens of ''Encephalartos woodii'' are [[cloning|clones]] of the [[endling|only known male plant]] which was completely removed from the wild. For these reasons, the plant is considered [[extinct in the wild]].<ref name=IUCN/>

===Legislation===
As is the case with all members of the genus ''Encephalartos'', ''Encephalartos woodii'' is protected by both national and international legislation:<ref name="Plantzafrica"/>

In South Africa one requires a permit from Nature Conservation to move, sell, buy, donate, receive, cultivate and sell Endangered Flora and to own adult cycads.
On an international level all species and hybrids of ''Encephalartos'' are on [[CITES Appendix I|Appendix I]] of [[CITES]], the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora. This means that wild collected material may not be traded and for each and every artificially cultivated ''Encephalartos'' plant or piece of a plant or a cone or pollen or seed, being carried over an international border requires a CITES Export Permit issued by the authority of the exporting country, and a CITES Import Permit issued by the authority of the importing country.<ref name=Plantzafrica/>

==Reproduction and propagation==

===Vegetative reproduction===
''Encephalartos woodii'' [[vegetative reproduction|reproduces]] with rapidly growing [[Basal shoot|sucker]]s.<ref name=Plantzafrica/><ref name=Cycadpages/>

===Sexual reproduction===
Unless a female plant is found, ''E. woodii'' will never reproduce naturally. This species is known to form fertile hybrids with ''E. natalensis'', and a [[backcrossing]] technique can be used: if each offspring is subsequently crossed with ''E. woodii'' and the process is then repeated, after several generations, female offspring will be closer to what a female ''Encephalartos woodii'' would be like.<ref name=Plantzafrica/> However, genetic analysis of [[chloroplast]] DNA of F1 hybrids between ''E. woodii'' and ''E. natalensis'' showed that all chloroplasts are inherited from the female ''E. natalensis'',<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cafasso |first=D |last2=Cozzolino |first2=S |last3=Caputo |first3=P |last4=Luca |first4=P De |name-list-style=vanc |date=2001 |title=Maternal inheritance of plastids in Encephalartos Lehm. (Zamiaceae, Cycadales) |journal=Genome |volume=44 |issue=2 |pages=239–241 |doi=10.1139/g01-005}}</ref> indicating that multi-generational hybrid offspring would have ''E. natalensis'' chloroplasts and could never be "pure" ''E. woodii''.

===Distribution of hybrids===
Several [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]]s between ''E. woodii'' and other species of ''Encephalartos'' have been produced including:
* ''[[Encephalartos gratus]]'' x ''E. woodii'' at Lotus Land, California.<ref name="Lotusland"/>
* ''[[Encephalartos natalensis]]'' x ''E. woodii'' at [[Orto botanico di Palermo]] in Italy, and in various collections in South Africa and the United States.
* ''[[Encephalartos transvenosus]]'' x ''E. woodii'' in collections in South Africa and the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encephalartos transvenosus x woodii at Aloes in Wonderland |url=https://www.aloesinwonderland.com/plant-gallery/encephalartos-transvenosus-x-woodii |access-date=2022-09-30 |website=www.aloesinwonderland.com}}</ref>
* ''[[Encephalartos arenarius]] x E. woodii'' at Aloes in Wonderland, California.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encephalartos arenarius x woodii at Aloes in Wonderland |url=https://www.aloesinwonderland.com/plant-gallery/encephalartos-arenarius-x-woodii |access-date=2022-09-30 |website=www.aloesinwonderland.com}}</ref>
* ''[[Encephalartos horridus]] x E. woodii'' at Aloes in Wonderland, California.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encephalartos horridus x woodii at Aloes in Wonderland |url=https://www.aloesinwonderland.com/plant-gallery/encephalartos-horridus-x-woodii |access-date=2022-09-30 |website=www.aloesinwonderland.com}}</ref>
